$comment: P1-28 composed permissions (SEC-001 / SEC-002), checked by
scripts/ci/check-p1-28-access.mjs (validate:p1-28-access).
The least-privilege rule derives what a screen MAY require from the P1-24
operation register: every permission the operations reachable from that
screen declare. That derivation has one blind spot, and it is not a
theoretical one — it is WF-27, the trap this phase's contract archaeology
names as the fourth of the five riskiest contract facts.
A write can require a permission the OPERATION does not declare. The
application check passes on the operation's own code and a row-level policy
on the table it writes then refuses the statement. The register cannot show
that, because the register records what a route registers.
So the composition is recorded here — and the record is VERIFIED, not
trusted. For every row the gate opens the named migration, finds the named
policy statement, and requires that statement to contain
iam.has_permission('<permission>'). A row whose citation no longer holds is
a violation, so this file cannot become a place to park a permission a
screen wanted for some other reason.
This is deliberately NOT an allow-list of screens. It records a fact about
an OPERATION, and any screen that can reach that operation inherits it —
which is why a new evidence screen needs no entry here and a screen that
cannot reach the operation gets no licence from it.

composed.why: WF-27. The operation registers rec.reception.evidence.manage and the application check passes on that alone. Two of its eight evidence kinds write a RESTRICTED narrative row beside the envelope — a complaint's text into rec.complaint_details, a content item's description, declared value and currency into rec.vehicle_content_details — and both tables carry INSERT policies ending in iam.has_permission('iam.sensitive.view'). The refusal is a database 42501 mapped to ERR-IAM-001, a 403 at write time on a form the operator was allowed to open. The check-in wizard therefore resolves this capability like any other and the two restricted steps withhold their capture form without it.
